scenario.name: Rhino Security Labs, Datadog & AWS — IAM PassRole + Lambda CreateFunction Privilege Escalation & CloudTrail StopLogging
scenario.shortSubtitle: Rhino Security Labs · Datadog Security Labs · MITRE Cloud · iam:PassRole + lambda:CreateFunction · AdministratorAccess
scenario.overview: Imagine a modern glass office building where visitors check in with the front-desk receptionist, scan a badge at the lobby turnstile, and walk between glass-walled meeting rooms. In the sunlit office building lobby, an unbadged visitor talks past the front-desk receptionist and persuades the desk clerk to print a temporary building pass. In this real-world scenario, the intruder steps up to the lobby badge turnstile blending in with everyday guests, then leaves a telltale trail inside the reception sign-in logbook. When building security compares the receptionist sign-in sheet against the turnstile badge swipes across the glass offices, the unescorted hallway trail is exposed. In this scenario (T1098.001, Rhino Security Labs, Datadog & AWS, IAM PassRole + Lambda CreateFunction Privilege Escalation & CloudTrail StopLogging), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: passing a Privileged IAM Role to a Newly, then invoking the Lambda Function to Attach, then disabling AWS CloudTrail Auditing. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Passing a Privileged IAM Role to a Newly, then Invoking the Lambda Function to Attach, then Disabling AWS CloudTrail Auditing, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection pivots on CloudTrail telemetry correlated across the documented kill chain.

stages.title: IAM PASSROLE & MALICIOUS LAMBDA FUNCTION CREATION
stages.subtitle: Binding high-privilege LambdaAdminDeploymentRole to a new Python function via iam:PassRole
stages.description: In the sunlit office building lobby, an unbadged visitor talks past the front-desk receptionist and persuades the desk clerk to print a temporary building pass. Specifically in Step 1, the intruder steps up to the lobby badge turnstile blending in with everyday guests while everyday visitors and the front-desk receptionist go about their routine. Using the compromised ci-dev-deployer access key, the attacker runs Pacu’s iam__privesc_scan module, discovers that the user policy permits iam:PassRole on Resource: "*" alongside lambda:CreateFunction, and invokes aws lambda create-function (binding the existing over-privileged role arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/LambdaAdminDeploymentRole to a 10-line Python handler named metrics-health-sync-tmp). Why does AWS require iam:PassRole? Because compute services like Lambda, EC2, ECS, and Glue execute code using the IAM Role attached to them; if iam:PassRole is granted with a wildcard ("*"), any user who can create a compute resource can impersonate any role trusted by that service. In the documented CLOUDTRAIL CreateFunction exchange from Compromised Dev IAM User to Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap, Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap responds with RESP HTTP 201 Created (confirming that the LAMBDA_CREATE_WITH_PASSROLE request succeeded on Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap and establishing the runtime state required for Step #2 LAMBDA INVOCATION & ADMINISTRATORACCESS POLICY ATTACHMENT). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ LAMBDA_CREATE_WITH_PASSROLE / ⇠#1 RESP HTTP 201 Created) from Node ① (#1 Compromised Dev IAM User) to Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 CloudTrail Lake & Datadog Cloud SIEM).

stages.title: LAMBDA INVOCATION & ADMINISTRATORACCESS POLICY ATTACHMENT
stages.subtitle: Executing boto3 iam.attach_user_policy(AdministratorAccess) inside the Lambda execution role
stages.description: Instead of staying in the public waiting chairs, the visitor taps that pass at the lobby turnstile and walks down the hallway from one glass meeting room to the next. Here in Step 2 inside the office building, the intruder bypasses the normal inspection rule to reach the executive glass meeting room without disturbing the public lobby waiting area. The attacker triggers the function via aws lambda invoke --function-name metrics-health-sync-tmp. Inside the AWS Lambda Firecracker microVM, the Python runtime automatically receives temporary STS credentials for LambdaAdminDeploymentRole in its environment variables and executes boto3.client("iam").attach_user_policy(UserName="ci-dev-deployer", PolicyArn="arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AdministratorAccess") (permanently elevating the attacker’s IAM user to full AWS account administrator). In CloudTrail, the AttachUserPolicy call appears as originating from AssumedRole/LambdaAdminDeploymentRole/metrics-health-sync-tmp rather than directly from the ci-dev-deployer IAM user. In the documented CLOUDTRAIL AttachUserPolicy exchange from Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap to AWS IAM & Lambda Control Plane, AWS IAM & Lambda Control Plane responds with ALERT GuardDuty High (confirming that the ADMIN_POLICY_ATTACHED request succeeded on AWS IAM & Lambda Control Plane and establishing the runtime state required for Step #3 CLOUDTRAIL STOPLOGGING DEFENSE EVASION). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ ADMIN_POLICY_ATTACHED / ⇠#2 ALERT GuardDuty High) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 AWS IAM & Lambda Control Plane), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 CloudTrail Lake & Datadog Cloud SIEM).

stages.title: CLOUDTRAIL STOPLOGGING DEFENSE EVASION
stages.subtitle: Halting regional CloudTrail audit recording via cloudtrail:StopLogging
stages.description: Inside the executive glass conference room, the intruder opens the unlocked cabinet and copies private project folders while staff walk by outside thinking they belong there. In this final step inside the office building, the intruder leaves a telltale trail inside the reception sign-in logbook until the reception sign-in logbook catches the mismatch. To conceal follow-on data theft or resource creation, the Lambda payload (or the newly elevated ci-dev-deployer user) calls boto3.client("cloudtrail").stop_logging(Name="org-audit-trail") (halting CloudTrail management and data event delivery for the regional trail, an action that records one final StopLogging event in CloudTrail and triggers GuardDuty’s Stealth:IAMUser/CloudTrailLoggingDisabled alert). Organizations prevent even full account administrators from blinding audit logs by configuring an AWS Organizations Trail in a separate management account and applying a Service Control Policy (SCP) that explicitly denies cloudtrail:StopLogging and cloudtrail:DeleteTrail. In the documented CLOUDTRAIL StopLogging exchange from AWS IAM & Lambda Control Plane to Lambda Execution MicroVM (Firecracker), Lambda Execution MicroVM (Firecracker) responds with ALERT TRAIL_STOPPED (confirming that the CLOUDTRAIL_LOGGING_DISABLED request succeeded on Lambda Execution MicroVM (Firecracker) and completing the final execution objective of Rhino Security Labs, Datadog & AWS, IAM PassRole + Lambda CreateFunction Privilege Escalation & CloudTrail StopLogging). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ CLOUDTRAIL_LOGGING_DISABLED / ⇠#3 ALERT TRAIL_STOPPED) from Node ③ (#3 AWS IAM & Lambda Control Plane) to Node ④ (#4 Lambda Execution MicroVM (Firecracker)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 CloudTrail Lake & Datadog Cloud SIEM).

detectionRule.title: AWS Lambda Function Created with High-Privilege IAM Role via PassRole
detectionRule.ruleCode:
title: Suspicious AWS Lambda CreateFunction with Admin Role
logsource:
  product: aws
  service: cloudtrail
detection:
  selection:
    eventSource: 'lambda.amazonaws.com'
    eventName: 'CreateFunction20150331'
    requestParameters.role|contains: 'Admin'
  condition: selection
detectionRule.mitigation: Scope iam:PassRole to specific non-admin role ARNs and require IAM Permissions Boundaries on all developer-created roles.

detectionRule.title: AWS IAM AdministratorAccess Policy Attached by Lambda Execution Role
detectionRule.ruleCode:
title: Lambda Execution Role Attaching AdministratorAccess Policy
logsource:
  product: aws
  service: cloudtrail
detection:
  selection:
    eventSource: 'iam.amazonaws.com'
    eventName: 'AttachUserPolicy'
    requestParameters.policyArn|endswith: ':policy/AdministratorAccess'
  condition: selection
detectionRule.mitigation: Never grant iam:AttachUserPolicy or iam:PutUserPolicy to compute execution roles (Lambda/EC2).

detectionRule.title: AWS CloudTrail Logging Disabled via StopLogging or DeleteTrail
detectionRule.ruleCode:
title: AWS CloudTrail StopLogging Invoked
logsource:
  product: aws
  service: cloudtrail
detection:
  selection:
    eventSource: 'cloudtrail.amazonaws.com'
    eventName:
      - 'StopLogging'
      - 'DeleteTrail'
  condition: selection
detectionRule.mitigation: Use an AWS Organizations Organization Trail managed in a dedicated Log Archive account and block cloudtrail:StopLogging via Service Control Policy (SCP).
